title: Efficiently Seeking Flat Minima for Better Generalization in Fine-Tuning Large Language Models and Beyond
publication_status_observed: AAAI 2026 (copyright line states Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence 2026; arXiv preprint arXiv:2508.00522v3)
main_claims: Perturbations in the full parameter space of LoRA can be theoretically re-parameterized as perturbations in a single low-rank subspace, avoiding interference between two matrices.
EFMLoRA achieves generalization improvements comparable to FMLoRA (full SAM on LoRA) with near-LoRA computational efficiency by using EMA-estimated perturbations.
Reducing sharpness is highly correlated with improved generalization in PEFT tasks, a connection previously unexplored for LoRA.
methodology: The authors derive a mathematical equivalence showing that SAM's full-parameter perturbation can be transferred to a single low-rank matrix (B) in LoRA. They propose FMLoRA (exact perturbation transfer) and EFMLoRA (EMA-based approximation). Experiments cover LLMs (RoBERTa-large, GPT-2) on GLUE/E2E and VLMs (CLIP, Qwen-VL-Chat) on SQA/VizWiz with multiple random seeds.
key_results: EFMLoRA outperforms LoRA by 1.0% average on GLUE benchmark with RoBERTa-large.
EFMLoRA achieves 1.5% and 1.0% improvements on SQA and VizWiz over LoRA for Qwen-VL-Chat.
EFMLoRA requires only 1.1–1.2× the runtime of LoRA versus FMLoRA's 2.1× overhead.
limitations: Theoretical analysis relies on approximations (pseudo-inverse, convexity assumption near local minimum) that may not hold in practice.
Experiments focus on NLP and VLM fine-tuning; no evaluation on CIFAR-C or image corruption benchmarks.
relevance_to_rq: This paper addresses SAM's mechanism in the LoRA context rather than OOD vision generalization. It is tangentially relevant as evidence that reducing sharpness correlates with generalization in fine-tuning settings, but does not address CIFAR-C OOD benchmarks or representation stability, making it peripheral to the RQ.
